Subject: Post-demo recommended model shortlist & tradeoffs for Stonebridge

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate you and Alan carving out time. Below is a concise post-demo recap and our recommended model shortlist with tradeoffs to help define the pilot.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):
- rw-balanced-8k-v2 (recommended): 8k context, best quality/latency balance for document QA. Expected latency: 120-160ms/token median on our Dedicated GPU; p99 ~ 1.6s for 512-token requests. Estimated unit cost: $0.020/token (hosted pricing) — see benchmarks.
- rw-lowcost-quant2-4bit: quantized variant for throughput and cost (approx 40-55% lower cost). Good for high-volume summary and short-answer workflows; tradeoff: modest drop in factuality on very long, domain-specific prompts. Latency: slightly lower median; p99 tail varies by prompt length.
- rw-highperf-16k-v1: larger-context, higher quality on multi-doc synthesis; higher cost and higher p99 latency but better handling of long-recall prompts. Good as fall-back for critical, high-complexity queries.

Attachments & links:
- stonebridge_benchmarks_20261201.pdf (benchmark summary: latency, cost, evals)
- stonebridge_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (sample prompts, expected outputs, evaluation targets)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExample

Quality/regression concerns:
- We flagged two prompt archetypes (multi-doc merge and jurisdiction-specific legal snippets) that show sensitivity to quantization: these are included in the prompt pack with evaluation thresholds.
- Recommended acceptance criteria for pilot: >92% top-answer precision on the provided prompt set; p99 latency <3.0s for 512-token flows at pilot throughput.

Next steps:
1) Confirm pilot scope (number of users / qps targets) and whether Stonebridge will supply a 3–5k sample corpus for domain validation.
2) We'll run a 7-day “pilot run” on Dedicated capacity using rw-balanced-8k-v2 and rw-lowcost-quant2-4bit and deliver a short validation report.
3) Internal: Ben will prepare a tightened latency-tail breakdown and Monica will produce an ops runbook for canary rollouts.

If this looks right, can we lock a follow-up next-week to align on pilot SLA and data access? I can share a DocuSign for the pilot TOS if legal is ready.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Maria — quick notes to address your questions, and copying Monica for pilot ops coordination.

On p99 for quantized (rw-lowcost-quant2-4bit):
- At ~25 qps simulated on our Dedicated 1xA100 pool with batching profile similar to your demo (avg prompt length ~320 tokens): median token latency ~95ms, p95 ~0.95s, p99 observed ~2.6–3.1s depending on load shaping and KV-cache hit rate. The higher end correlates with cache misses on multi-doc lookups.

Quality regression on legal/jurisdiction prompts:
- We ran a small canonicalization test included in the prompt pack. Typical delta: top-answer precision drops ~4–6 percentage points versus rw-balanced-8k-v2 on long, citation-heavy prompts. For short Q/A (<50 tokens) the delta is negligible. We've annotated 6 sample prompts in stonebridge_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl that show the largest delta.

Operational mitigations:
- Canary policy: route 5–10% of legal/jurisdiction flows to rw-highperf-16k-v1 as a fallback.
- Threshold gating: require >90% precision on incoming daily sample to auto-promote quantized variant.

Attachment: latency_tail_breakdown.csv (CSV with p50/p95/p99 by model and prompt archetype)

If helpful I can surface the raw p99 traces in the Drive link — let me know and I'll drop them to the shared folder.

Thanks,
